exercise.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand

reference.title: Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip, knee and ankle; step-up from half-kneeling)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in while kneeling and before each step; exhale as you drive up to standing; breathe in again before lowering back down.
breathing.cadence: About 3 s from kneeling to standing, 3 s back down

prescription.tempo: Controlled; pause in half-kneeling and when standing
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can hold at the chest through every rep with good posture (RPE 6-8).
prescription.progression: Slower lowering, then a heavier dumbbell; alternate the lead leg each rep

cues.text: Kneel tall on a mat, knees hip width, toes tucked; hold one dumbbell upright at the chest, elbows down, ribs down.
Shift onto the left knee and step the right foot forward, foot flat, front shin about vertical: half-kneeling.
Breathe out and drive through the front foot to stand, chest up; step the back foot up beside the front one.
Breathe in, step the left foot back onto its ball and lower the knee softly to the mat; then bring the right foot back.
Tall kneeling again, dumbbell still at the chest; repeat, leading with the same or the other leg.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the back knee onto the floor
mistakes.fix: Lower it slowly; use a mat or pad under the knees.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing off the back foot instead of the front
mistakes.fix: Drive through the whole front foot; the back leg only steadies you.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far forward or rounding the back
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest up and the dumbbell close to the sternum; a small forward lean is fine.
Keep the knee in line with the toes as you stand.
Keep the feet about hip width apart side to side for balance.

kinematics.setup: Tall kneeling: knees 18 cm apart, hips 3° (thighs about vertical), toes tucked
kinematics.peak: Half-kneeling: front knee ≈109°, rear knee ≈111° on the floor
kinematics.norm: Tall kneeling with the thighs about vertical; half-kneeling with both knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees in half-kneeling, nearly straight standing (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Up to ≈7° forward while driving up
kinematics.norm: Upright when kneeling and standing; a small forward lean while driving up (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Upright at the sternum, hands cupping the top plate
kinematics.peak: Clear of the chest and thighs (≥2.63 cm on the rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Held upright at the sternum throughout (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.25 s step to half-kneeling, 1.75 s up and step in, 1 s standing, 3.2 s back down, 0.8 s kneeling
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 3 s up and 3 s down with pauses in half-kneeling and standing (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11217, Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand, video (movement reference; page not readable here)

cautions: Kneel on a mat or folded towel to protect the knees.
Knee pain when kneeling: skip the tall-kneeling part and start from half-kneeling on a thicker pad.
Choose a dumbbell you can hold close to the chest without the elbows flaring; the load is user-chosen.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Balance: rest one hand on a bench or wall and hold the dumbbell in the other hand, or do it without the dumbbell.
Tight ankles: keep the toes tucked and the steps shorter.
regressions: Body-weight kneel to stand with a hand on a bench.
Half-kneeling to stand only (start with one foot forward).
progressions: Turkish get-up for the full floor-to-standing pattern.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors drive the rise from half-kneeling and control the way down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; drives the rise with the quadriceps (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Rear-leg knee extensors help as the knee leaves the floor and in the split stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the rear hip extended in tall and half-kneeling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Assist hip extension of the front leg.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push the rear foot onto its ball in the split stance.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright under the dumbbell through every position change.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steady the pelvis on the narrow kneeling base and in the split stance.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steady the pelvis on the narrow kneeling base and in the split stance.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Hold the dumbbell at the chest.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the dumbbell at the chest.

guides.label: Drive up over the front foot
